subject: PaxCredit priority: reserved throughput ceiling breach — summit call and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Ashley Nguyen <ashley@paxcredit.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: tom.rios@paxcredit.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency and errors on Redwood Dedicated — PaxCredit production

Marcus / Hannah,

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and long tail latency around 07:00 PT this morning — impacting our loan-approval flow (affects ~8% of requests). Latency 99.9th jumped from ~320ms to >1.4s and error rate spiked to ~2.7%. Our dashboard shows requests routed to your dedicated GPU pool (reserved).

This is customer-impacting for our Premium loan cohort. We need an estimated time to mitigation and whether a temporary fallback to a hosted model variant (lower throughput but stable) is possible while you remediate. Please advise next steps and timeline; we are standing by for a call.

Thanks,
Ashley Nguyen
Head of Core Platform
PaxCredit

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and errors on Redwood Dedicated — PaxCredit production

Ashley — thanks for the flag and sample. We’re opening an incident. Quick status:

- Triage team (Karthik + infra) looking at pool headroom and scheduler logs now.
- Early signal: sustained queue depth increase on the reserved pool that matches PaxCredit token distribution around 07:00 PT.
- We’ll propose mitigation options in the next 30 min and request a 1 PM PT executive/technical summit to align on trade-offs.

Can you confirm whether the affected route uses pinned model v2.3 (quantized) or the fallback v2.2? That helps us choose the right fallback.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and errors on Redwood Dedicated — PaxCredit production

Quick infra readout (from scheduler + host metrics):

- Dedicated pool pax-reserved-04 reached a sustained concurrency level that triggered continuous batching fallback at ~07:03 PT. Batching behaviour caused queue growth for short-lived low-latency requests.
- One of the NVLink hosts reported elevated kernel retire counts and GPU memory churn (likely KV cache thrash) after a sudden burst of long context requests from PaxCredit’s pipeline.
- We see autoscale did not add new hosts because load signaled across other reserved customers in the same isolation tier; our policy avoided cross-tenant bursting.

Immediate mitigations proposed (ranked):
1) Emergency soft-pin: route PaxCredit traffic to a dedicated overflow pool (hot-swap) + increase worker count (fastest; needs approval to borrow headroom from shared burst).
2) Canary fallback: switch PaxCredit route to v2.2 (lower memory) for 30m window — reduces tail but increases token cost slightly.
3) Client-side throttling: reduce PaxCredit client concurrency by 20% while we remediate (requires their deployment change).

I’ll prepare a short MAP (mitigation + action plan) and attach traces. We need exec sign-off on option 1 or 2.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Ashley Nguyen <ashley@paxcredit.com>, Tom Rios <tom.rios@paxcredit.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: PaxCredit — immediate options and 1pm PT summit invite

Ashley / Tom — apologies for the disruption. Short summary and asks before the 13:00 PT summit:

Summary of fault: reserved pool overflow + KV-cache churn for large context requests from PaxCredit. This created queueing which resulted in elevated tail latency and 5xxs.
Immediate options (trade-offs):
- Option A (preferred by infra): Emergency soft-pin to overflow pool (we temporarily borrow burst capacity). Pros: fastest reduction in errors and tail latency. Cons: small chance to affect SLAs for other burst-eligible customers; ops approval required.
- Option B (customer-side safe): Canary fallback to v2.2 for 30 minutes. Pros: no cross-tenant capacity shift; likely reduces memory pressure. Cons: slightly higher token cost for PaxCredit and small difference in output quality.
- Option C: Client throttling (20% concurrency cap) — reduce throughput until backend stabilization. Pros: no infra changes. Cons: degrades PaxCredit throughput and may impact client SLAs.

Asks:
1) Can PaxCredit accept Option B for an initial 30-minute canary? This is the lowest-risk from a platform policy perspective.
2) Redwood execs: Hannah / David — we need a quick sign-off to apply Option A if Option B does not restore service within 30m.

I’ve attached the MAP-action-items-20280605.xlsx (first tab: immediate runbook) and prod-traces-20280604.zip. Please join the 1pm PT summit (calendar invite attached).

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive — Priority GTM
From: Ashley Nguyen <ashley@paxcredit.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: tom.rios@paxcredit.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PaxCredit — immediate options and 1pm PT summit invite

Marcus / team — we ran Option B (canary to v2.2) at ~10:10 PT and saw immediate improvement: 99.9th dropped to ~360ms and errors returned to baseline within 12 minutes. We’ll stay on v2.2 for now while you validate.

A couple of asks after the summit outcome:
- ETA to restore v2.3 safely with prewarming or cache warming steps?
- If you need to borrow burst headroom (Option A) during a future surge, we want the communication and rollback SLAs spelled out.
- We’ll need a post-incident report with root cause and mitigations (including scheduler policy change options).

Thanks for the rapid response — appreciate the escalation.

Ashley
Head of Core Platform, PaxCredit
